slots.title: Fed’s Collins backs gradual rate hikes
slots.body:
Fed’s Collins: gradual rate hikes are the best way to manage economic risks — per Reuters on Nov. 14.

That framing matters because “gradual hikes” means the central bank would raise its policy rate in small steps rather than large jumps, which changes how fast loans, mortgages, and business borrowing costs can move.

Treasury yields in the injected snapshot (Nov. 12): 10-year at 5.1%, 2-year at 4.9%, 2s–10s spread at 0.24.

Prior session risk gauge: CBOE Volatility Index $VIX +3.2% to 19.30.

Which Fed speaker headline are you tracking this weekend — hikes, inflation, or something else?

slots.title: Chicago Fed: missing on inflation
slots.body:
Chicago Fed President Goolsbee: the Fed is “failing on the inflation side of the dual mandate” — the dual mandate is maximum employment plus stable prices (inflation near target).

He said inflation has run above target for three or four months and is moving the wrong way in categories that are hard to reverse quickly.

He linked part of the pressure to AI data-center build-out, calling it a historically large stimulus that can push demand above what the economy can smoothly absorb (“overheating”).

Prior US index close (Nov. 14): S&P 500 $SPX −0.4% to 7,561.67.

Nasdaq Composite $COMP −0.9% to 25,136.27.

When Fed officials talk inflation miss, what data print do you watch first — consumer prices, jobs, or something else?

slots.title: US close — Nov. 14, 2026
slots.body:
The Nasdaq Composite led the decline among major US indexes, closing at 25,136.27, down 0.9% (229.82 points), with an intraday range between 24,872.41 and 25,423.09.
